RULE — all six obligations of GR24, each re-derived on this tree, never inherited: (a) 'When the value of a specific alternate record key is not changed, the order of retrieval when that key is the key of reference remains unchanged' (cite.py --check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (b) 'When the value of a specific alternate record key is changed … the record is logically positioned last within the set of duplicate records where the alternate record key value is equal to the same alternate key value in one or more records in the file based on the collating sequence for the file' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (c) the FIRST SUPPRESS WHEN sub-rule, 'If the SUPPRESS WHEN phrase is specified in the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause and the value of the alternate record key is no longer equal to the literal specified in that phrase: 1. an access path to this record using this key of reference shall be provided, and 2. the record shall be logically positioned so that it will be found when accessed using the alternate record key' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (d) the SECOND SUPPRESS WHEN sub-rule, 'If alternate record key suppression is specified for this alternate record key and the value of this alternate record key is now equal to its key suppression value: 1. the access path to the record using this alternate record key shall no longer be provided, and 2. the record shall be logically repositioned so that it will not be found when accessed using this alternate record key' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (e) 'The comparison used for determining changes to the key is based on the collating sequence for the file according to the rules for a relation condition' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (f) 'Any number of records may have the same alternate key value equal to its key suppression value without requiring the DUPLICATES phrase to be specified for that key. Key entries that are suppressed shall not cause a duplicate key condition to exist' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)). CODE: IndexedConnector.Rewrite runs TWO passes over _alts and the order is load-bearing — pass 1 validates only (an early '22' must leave nothing repositioned), pass 2 applies GR24 while target.Image is still the REPLACED record so AltChanged compares against it. (a)/(b): the local AltChanged(i) is the ONE definition of 'this REWRITE changed alternate key i', and only the keys it answers true for take a fresh release ordinal off the monotone mint (Stamp(target, i, repositioned)), so an untouched key keeps its ordinal and IndexedConnector.SelectSequentialRecord(i) keeps its order, while a changed key sorts after every existing member of its new duplicate set. (e): AltChanged is KeyEq, the file's collating sequence, not an ordinal string compare. (c)/(d): AltChanged also returns true when IndexedConnector.AlternateValue(image, i) != IndexedConnector.AlternateValue(target.Image, i), so entering OR leaving suppression is a change of its own and re-stamps the key; the access path itself is IndexedConnector.SelectSequentialRecord(keyIndex)'s Where(r => !IndexedConnector.AlternateValue(r.Image, keyIndex)) (12.4.5.6.4 GR6), which withdraws and restores the path from the key VALUE with no separate state to drift. (f): pass 1 does `if (IndexedConnector.AlternateValue(image, i)) continue;` before the uniqueness test and also excludes suppressed records from the `exists` scan, so a suppressed entry can neither raise '22' on a non-DUPLICATES key nor be duplicated by one. MEASURED on this worktree's build (c34f01ad + this change) by conformance:cases/14.9.35-REWRITE/l1_rewrite_alt_key_suppress, whose 20 expected lines were WRITTEN FROM THE SPEC BEFORE THE FIRST RUN and matched byte for byte: leg B REWRITEs record 01's R-A1 to the suppression value 'XX' and the R-A1 walk drops from 01,03,02 to 03,02 at status '00' (d); leg C REWRITEs it back to 'AA' and the walk becomes 03,01,02 — the access path is restored (c 1.) and 01, which was FIRST in the AA set on release, comes back LAST (c 2. + b), with the REWRITE itself reporting '02' per 9.1.13.2 2 c); leg D REWRITEs two records to 'ZZ', the suppression value of an alternate key with NO DUPLICATES phrase, and both report '00' rather than the '22' a real duplicate would raise, after which the R-A2 walk finds only the one unsuppressed record (f); leg E re-walks after CLOSE/OPEN and both the restored position and the two withdrawn paths survive the physical file. conformance:cases/9.1.13.2-Successful-completion/l1_rewrite_alt_key_order (kb/Work PB341) independently pins (a), (b) and (e) on two DUPLICATES alternate keys without suppression. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 85 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 for (a), (b) and (e) — ALTERNATE RECORD KEY and its DUPLICATES phrase are ungated in this compiler (no constructs.json row), the clause carries no edition marker, and Annex E lists no change to 14.9.35; this matches the band the sibling rows GR-14.9.30.4-26 and GR-14.9.30.4-32 were landed at on the same golden. Sub-rules (c), (d) and (f) are 2023-ONLY: they exist only where SUPPRESS WHEN is writable, and SUPPRESS WHEN is a COBOL-2023 addition (cite.py --check E.3.3 'The SUPPRESS WHEN phrase may be specified as part of the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause' -> OK, item 42), gated by constructs.json row 'alternate-key-suppress-when-2023' (COBOL0900 below 2023) — so the 2023 golden is the only edition at which they CAN be measured, and they are vacuous, not unverified, at 85/2002/2014. || kb/Work PB2693 (w1045d): the release ordinals are PERSISTED with each record and the release mint in the store header (store format 4), so every key's duplicate order survives a CLOSE/OPEN even when no single record order carries them all (the PB701 cyclic residue is gone), and a coherent reload after another run unit's DELETE no longer renumbers them, which made a duplicate walk skip a record. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/IndexedConnector.cs#PersistOrder (kb/Work PB2693 deleted the topological persist order: each record's release ordinals are persisted with it (store format 4), so the file order decides nothing)
